predictions.reasoning: Howard Lutnick (Commerce Secretary, ex-Cantor Fitzgerald CEO) is closely tied to the crypto ecosystem via Cantor's custody relationship with Tether and its Bitcoin-related SPAC dealings. His presence in the administration is seen as crypto-friendly. A sharp rise in his departure probability could modestly dent sentiment around a pro-crypto regulatory stance, but the linkage is indirect, policy is institutionalized beyond one official, and the direction is genuinely ambiguous (a departure could be read either way). Magnitude far below the 700bps tradable threshold.

predictions.reasoning: As Commerce Secretary, Lutnick is a central figure in tariff and trade negotiations. A surprise departure could raise short-term uncertainty about trade-policy continuity, but Trump sets trade direction himself, so a single secretary's exit is a weak driver of the broad index. Mapping is too diffuse to produce a reliable directional 12h signal, and well below tradable magnitude.

llm_justification.summary: This market asks whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick leaves before 2027. The only plausible public-market linkages run through his crypto-industry ties (via Cantor/Tether) and his role in trade policy, but both channels are indirect and directionally ambiguous. A sharp probability move would be a weak, noisy signal; expected asset moves are far below the 700bps tradable threshold. Best characterized as unclear with low confidence — this is research, not an actionable edge.

Trade/tariff policy continuity is partly attributed to his presence
Prediction-market probability shifts here can precede public confirmation

Proxy exposure (IBIT/SPY) to one cabinet official is very weak
Direction reverses — a Lutnick exit could be read as bullish or bearish for crypto
Any observed asset move is driven by unrelated macro catalysts, creating false attribution
